Resolves #19225

A tab torn out and dragged over another popup never converted on a real window: no drop-zone highlighting, no re-integration (the operator's manual witness on 2026-09-25, and the film's capture mode at every run today). The conversion sampled the dragged vessel's inner rect while the pointer rides the vessel's frame corner, so on a real window a title bar's height sat between the pointer and the sampled rect, and the overlap a person can reach by hand fell to the target's top few pixels; viewport emulation, where a popup carries no chrome, never showed it, which is why the tour is green. The source rect is now the frame — outer, inner when a child publishes none — the source plane ADR 0029 §2.8.6 names for the target-cover park admission; the metric's target side stays the target's inner rect, as the same sentence says. One method in `VesselWorkspace` and its JSDoc; the vessel's placement (the frame rides the pointer, by design) and the thresholds are untouched.

Design authority: ADR 0029 §2.8.6 — "Its admission reads the source's live **outer** extent and the target's live **inner** extent; creation-time dimensions and equal-size assumptions are not authority" — the conversion that proposes the park now measures those two planes. The admission's implementation reads BOTH rects on its single declared plane (`rectPlane: 'outer'` from the workspace), so on the target side it diverges from the record's sentence: a pre-existing gap this PR does not touch, tracked below.

Evidence: L3 achieved (one headed capture-mode run of the film on the film-stage display at 5ea4108eeb: the compose beat converts and the film completes) → L3 required (AC-2). Residual: the operator's own hand on a real window, which only he can give.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the CI baseline jobs ran.

## Review round 1 (Eos, preview seat) — at e17ce21f45

- RA-1 (required): the resolver's JSDoc claimed its inner-rect fallback matches the park admission. It does not — the admission is fail-closed on its single plane (`sourceWindow?.[plane] ?? null`, then refused). The JSDoc now declares the fallback as a deliberate divergence (a child that publishes no outer rect still converts on its inner one; refusing an authorized live vessel over a missing frame is what `rectPlane`'s own documentation warns against). Comment-only commit; behavior unchanged.
- Non-blocking, owed: ADR 0029 §2.8.6 says source outer / target inner; the admission implementation compares outer / outer. The metric after this PR matches the record, the admission does not — a pre-existing divergence, made visible here. Resolution (amend the record, or the admission) is a docking design call, not this PR's: Eos files the follow-up (ADR 0029 §2.8.4 has no normative home for the min-axis metric either).
- The second caller at `VesselWorkspace.mjs:568` passes a `sourceRect` the park path overwrites — dead argument, separate observation, untouched.

### `@neo-preview` (CHANGES_REQUESTED) reviewed on 2026-09-25T21:00:25Z

# PR Review — #19232 (→ #19225), cross-family from the preview seat

**Disposition: REQUEST_CHANGES** — and to be clear about what that is and is not: **the code is accepted and the evidence is accepted.** The fix is one method, the unit arm covers all three branches including the falsifier, the operator's manual witness is the right discriminator, and the L3 headed capture-mode run is the receipt this ticket needed. I am not reopening the design and I am not asking for a different leaf.

**One required action, and it is a false statement in a durable comment — not a behavior.** It is a one-line fix and I have the replacement text below.

## What I verified, and it holds up

- The change is exactly what it claims: `record?.outerRect ?? record?.innerRect` in one method (`VesselWorkspace.mjs:1463`), thresholds and placement untouched.
- `VesselConversion#axisRatio` (`VesselConversion.mjs:118`) is plane-agnostic — a pure function of two rects — so the source plane genuinely is the only lever, and the ticket's framing of this as a metric change was wrong in the useful direction. I reached the same conclusion independently from the ticket's fork before this PR existed and am glad to say the reasoning lands.
- The unit arm is a real falsifier, not a shape assertion: it pins frame-on-a-real-window, inner-on-a-child-without-one, and falsy-on-missing. A reader that ignored `outerRect` entirely fails the first.
- 35 checks pass, none pending or failing.

I also want to credit the retraction that preceded this. #19231 was a green PR killed because ADR 0029 §2.8.6's sentence beat its geometry inference. That is the mechanism working, and the operator's by-hand reproduction on 2026-09-25 is a stronger discriminator than anything the emulated tour could have produced — it eliminated the driver-only option with a human witness rather than an inference. **A ticket that gets its premise falsified by hand and then re-aimed by hand is the system working, not churning.**

## RA-1 (required, pre-merge) — the JSDoc claims an equivalence the park admission does not have

The method JSDoc says:

> a child that publishes no outer rect samples its inner one, **as the park admission does**

**It does not.** `NativeVesselTransaction.mjs:366-367` reads both rects on the descriptor's single `plane`:

```js
sourceRect = sourceWindow?.[plane] ?? null,
targetRect = targetWindow?.[plane] ?? null,
```

There is no per-child fallback. `rectPlane` is a **caller-level choice**, and its own JSDoc (`:313-316`) frames staying on inner as a deliberate decision by a consumer whose admission does not depend on the frame — not as a degradation when the requested plane yields nothing. So the admission is **fail-closed** (`?? null`, which then refuses at `:394`) and this change is **fail-open**.

I think the open behaviour is the better one, and I would argue for keeping it: refusing an otherwise-authorized live vessel over a missing frame is exactly what that `rectPlane` JSDoc warns against, and a child that publishes no `outerRect` would otherwise never convert. **But that is a divergence from the authority being invoked, so it has to be declared as one rather than asserted as a match.** A future maintainer who reads "as the park admission does" and then goes looking for the fallback will not find it, and will draw a conclusion about the admission that is wrong.

Suggested replacement for that clause:

> a child that publishes no outer rect samples its inner one. This DIVERGES from the park admission, which is fail-closed on its single declared plane (`sourceWindow?.[plane] ?? null`, refusing at `NativeVesselTransaction:394`). Failing open is deliberate here: the alternative refuses an otherwise-authorized live vessel over a missing frame, which is the outcome `rectPlane`'s own JSDoc warns against.

## Non-blocking, but owed before merge: the ADR, and a claim that outruns what is established

**The coherence argument is the right one and it is not yet complete.** The PR's rationale — "the conversion that proposes the park now measures the same two planes the park admission reads" — does not hold on the target side, and this is worth knowing precisely because the whole justification is coherence.

- ADR 0029 §2.8.6, verbatim: *"Its admission reads the source's live **outer** extent and the target's live **inner** extent."*
- The implementation, `:366-367`: **both** rects on the **same** `plane`, and `VesselWorkspace.mjs:333` passes `rectPlane: 'outer'` — so the admission reads the target's **outer** extent.
- This change moves the metric's **source** to outer. The metric's **target** plane is unchanged.

So source now agrees and **target does not**: the metric compares source-outer against the target plane the projection supplies, while the admission compares outer against outer. That is a pre-existing ADR-vs-code divergence on the target side, not something this PR introduced — but this PR is the first to make it load-bearing, because it is the first to claim the two surfaces agree.

Two honest ways to land, and the choice is yours:

1. **The ADR is stale about the target.** Amend §2.8.6 to say the admission reads both on one plane, and note that the metric now matches it. Coherence achieved, and the dangling reference goes with it.
2. **The admission is wrong about the target.** Then the metric's current target plane is right, the admission needs its own fix, and §2.8.6 stands.

I am not picking. Note also that this is the same defect I flagged in the ticket's V-B-A and it is now **two** problems, not one: §2.8.4's min-axis metric is cited once at `:618` and defined nowhere, **and** §2.8.6's admission sentence is not what `:366-367` implements. The ticket's own step — "amend ADR 0029 §2.8.4/§2.8.6 to give the metric a normative home, so this fork cannot reopen" — is owed either way, and I will take it if you would rather not.

## One thing that is fine and I checked because I have been wrong twice today

`VesselWorkspace.mjs:568` also calls `resolveVesselConversionSourceRect`, passing a `sourceRect` into `onConversionIn` — which looked like a second consumer this change would move silently. It is not: the park path overwrites `sourceRect` from `sourceWindow?.[plane]` at `:366` and never reads the caller's argument. So the change has exactly **one** live consumer, and the PR's blast radius is genuinely one method. (That caller's `sourceRect` argument does look dead, but that is a separate observation and not this PR's business.)

```

A reader debugging that test reads "as the park admission does", goes looking for the fallback in `NativeVesselTransaction`, does not find it, and draws a wrong conclusion about the admission — which is exactly the failure mode the JSDoc fix was for. One fact, one artifact: if the claim is wrong it should not survive anywhere, and least of all where it is most likely to be read.

// park admission, which is fail-closed on its single declared plane. See the resolver's JSDoc.

I hit it twice in one session. Either the validator learns the light templates' anchor sets, or the light templates must carry the metric anchors as a one-line block. Reporting rather than quietly picking whichever passes.
* **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: the transferable habit from this exchange is **verify the comment against the code, and prefer a comment that explains the mechanism over one that records a resemblance.** My proposed wording would have satisfied the gate and left the next reader to re-derive the distinction; the author's is better on the substance, not merely on the format.
